title: Split a capture from a Visa link into frames

blocks.text: The support desk wants to see what Visa's side of a link really sends, frame by frame, instead of what the application logged after unpacking. A small pass-through will sit on the connection: it reads everything the network sends and hands each frame to the desk as two byte arrays, the header bytes and the message bytes. Because it sits on a live link, it has to treat everything that arrives the way jPOS's `VAPChannel` does, or the link suffers.
`Base1Frames` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Base1Frames.java` already reads the prefixes and returns the frames. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `poll`: what to do with a prefix that has no message behind it;
`readHeaders`: every header byte in front of the message, on any frame the network may send;

cases.says: a frame comes out as its header bytes and its message bytes, and the capture then ends
frames that follow each other come out one by one, in order
a frame with length zero is no message and is written back to the network as it came
a reject header and the original header behind it are both read as header, whatever their lengths
the prefix's length counts every header byte, so a message ends where its frame ends even behind a longer header

origin.section: 5.2. A Rejected Message Comes Back Behind a Longer Header, With No Field 39

concepts: On a BASE I link a four-byte prefix and a header come before the MTI; the header's first byte gives its length, and the prefix's length counts the header as well as the message.
A frame with length zero is a poll, not a message, and VAPChannel writes it back to the network.
A network reject returns the sender's own message behind a longer reject header, with no field 39; the refusal and its code are in the header.
